findings.summary: Pre-existing, narrowed by this PR. When --repo-root IS the shared main checkout (non-worktree usage, or reconciling from the main checkout), the fallback in determineVerdictClass credits a role-matched marker under repoRoot as independent/attested with a null hash and no nonce check. Task B can therefore be credited off task A's same-role reviewer marker and consume it. On main this was worse: any reviewer-role marker in the window, no role binding. Not a regression. Follow-up: once every caller passes --nonce, require a nonce-verified marker for independent everywhere and retire the local role-and-timing rule.

findings.summary: The fallback snippet de-duplicates by agentId and only refuses when more than one marker is found. With exactly one marker of the role present belonging to another task (this task's reviewer wrote none, or it was already consumed), it returns that task's id. persist-reviewer-artifacts.sh then copies the other task's harness transcript in as this task's, and emit-leaf produces a self-authored leaf with a null hash whose transcriptHash covers the other task's review. The class correctly flags it, so this is an integrity nuisance rather than a way to get credit. Minimal hardening: before persisting, check that the resolved harness transcript contains $PR_NONCE_MARKER (or pass the nonce to the persist helper and have it refuse).

findings.summary: Pre-existing TOCTOU, not worsened: the marker is consumed with a best-effort unlink after the candidate checks, so two concurrent emit-leaf runs for the same leaf identity can both bind and both report independent. The same read-then-unlink pattern is on main. Cross-task double use is impossible because it needs both nonces in one transcript. Suggestion: claim the marker atomically (renameSync to a per-process name, or open with O_EXCL on a .consumed sibling) and grant independent only to the process that wins the claim.
